To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) EPI solution's acid pH increases the permeation through low thickness nitriles; 2) EPI can induce apoptosis in epithelial cell lines at concentrations lower than the one able to permeate through nitrile gloves; and 3) the choice of the appropriate glove type for preventing EPI occupational exposure is fundamental for reducing the risk of skin toxicity.
the EPI permeability of various commercial gloves was evaluated and the effects on human keratynocyte cell line were investigated.
EPI permeates nitrile gloves and induces apoptosis in epithelial cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies to prevent the occupational exposure to anticancer drugs, with the ultimate goal of improving the safety conditions of health care professionals.
the development of an integrated approach for the risk assessment of EPI occupational exposure.
the development of a useful and effective tool for assessing the risk of skin damage due to EPI exposure and for the choice of appropriate PPE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of gloves with low permeation to EPI is strongly recommended.
the choice of a glove should not be made solely on the basis of permeation results but also on toxicity data.
the use of nitrile gloves with low thickness, as well as the use of EPI in acid form should be strictly avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EPI permeation of nitrile glove can induce apoptosis in human epithelial cells, which is an important finding for understanding the toxicological effects of this antitumor drug.
, when EPI is handled, gloves should be used, and that the choice of the most appropriate glove is crucial to prevent occupational exposure to this drug.
EPI permeation of personal protection equipment can induce apoptosis and that the pH of EPI solution is an important parameter to be taken into account in order to prevent the occupational exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when using nitrile gloves, the risk of EPI skin absorption is high and should be considered in occupational settings where the drug is used.
, even at concentrations lower than 0.1 mg/L, EPI can induce apoptosis through the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, independently from the presence of p53.
, when EPI is handled in the form of neutral solution, the risk of skin exposure can be considered negligible.
